speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a distal obstruction with no gas in the rectum, which is highly concerning for Hirschsprung's disease given the failure to pass meconium and bilious vomiting. Since the home birth lacked prenatal screening, I need to know if there are any other siblings with similar bowel issues or if the infant has had any feeding difficulties beyond the vomiting. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung's disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy results confirming the absence of ganglion cells are diagnostic for Hirschsprung's disease. Given the clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and distal obstruction on imaging, I have sufficient evidence.
